purpose: Teach: 漱石/空軍/レジャー/ヘリコプター/スタディ/ベクトル/マンハッタン/マダム

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前、現代文で漱石やったろ?
lines.en: Riku, didn't you cover Soseki in modern literature?
lines.style: Casual, direct challenge masked as genuine question. Sharp lift on his name. Testing whether he's been paying attention in class.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、空軍に憧れてんのか?桜
lines.en: What, are you secretly into the air force or something, Sakura?
lines.style: Deflecting with a counter-question. Light sarcasm underneath. Turning her curiosity back on her with a small smile in the voice.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前のレジャープラン教えてくれよ
lines.en: So come on, what are you actually planning to do on your time off?
lines.style: Pressing harder now. Impatient but not unkind. She wants a real answer, not evasion. Direct eye contact level.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、テレビでヘリコプター見たろ?桜
lines.en: Did you see that helicopter thing on TV the other day?
lines.style: Casual sidestep. He's asking a question that sounds innocent but feels like a redirect. Quieter, less confrontational than before.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前、ケーススタディ得意なのか?
lines.en: Wait—are you actually good at case studies or something?
lines.style: Surprised, a little impressed. Quick rhythm. She's noticing something she didn't expect about him. Slight pitch lift on the opening.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、数学のベクトル、わかるか?桜
lines.en: Do you get vectors in math, Sakura? Like, actually understand them?
lines.style: Quiet, almost vulnerable underneath. He's asking because he doesn't understand them and wondering if she does. Not apologetic, just genuine.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前のお父さん、マンハッタン出張行ったろ?
lines.en: Hey, didn't your dad go to Manhattan for work recently?
lines.style: Shift in tone. Casual on the surface but genuinely interested. Remembering details she's mentioned. Making conversation that lands.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前のお母さん、マダムって感じだよな、桜
lines.en: Your mom's got this whole composed, elegant thing going on, doesn't she?
lines.style: Soft, reflective observation. Not gossiping—just noticing. A little admiring, maybe a touch wistful. Close enough to see her clearly.
